stages.title: THE CENTRAL QUESTION OF THE INDIVIDUAL-STATE RELATION AND ITS VOCABULARY
sequence: Why a state: scarcity, disagreement, risk of harm
Five purposes: order, rights, goods, justice, collective action
The protector itself can dominate
Justified, limited and answerable power
Legitimacy, not mere coercion

groups.heading: THE RELATION IN THREE IDEAS
items: Rights are justified claims, duties are what is owed, and accountability is power that must answer.
Rights without limits become licence, duties without rights become subordination, and power without answerability becomes domination.
The clause fixes a normative relation, not an institutional description of any particular constitution.

groups.heading: WHY A STATE, AND ON WHAT TERMS
items: Scarcity, disagreement and the risk of harm leave disputes without an impartial umpire.
The state supplies order and security, rights protection, public goods, justice and welfare, and collective action.
Legitimacy is a right to rule that subjects have reason to accept; a gang obtains obedience without ever acquiring it.

groups.heading: THE VOCABULARY THAT EARNS THE FIRST MARK
items: Individual, society, civil society, government and state are five different things and must not be run together.
Locate every stem on the spectrum from minimal through welfare and socialist to totalitarian and stateless.
Define the terms first, locate the case second, and adjudicate only at the end.

stages.mechanism_strip: Scarcity, disagreement and the risk of harm leave disputes without an impartial umpire, so a state is instituted to supply order and security, rights protection, public goods, justice and welfare, and the collective action no individual can achieve alone.
stages.answer_line: The individual and the state are related by justification and not by force: a state earns authority when it supplies order, rights protection, public goods, justice and collective action, and it keeps that authority only while it remains limited and answerable.

stages.title: GROUNDING A RIGHT: NATURE, LAW AND THE CRITICAL MORAL REGISTER

pills.text: NATURAL RIGHTS PRIOR TO THE STATE

sequence: A right is a justified claim, liberty, power or immunity
Natural ground: prior to the state, limits government
Legal ground: claimant, duty-bearer and remedy
Moral ground: criticism of a valid but unjust law
Verdict: nature grounds, law enforces, morality judges

groups.heading: THREE GROUNDS OF A RIGHT
items: Natural (Locke): rights are held in the state of nature — life, liberty and property — before any government exists.
Legal (Bentham): a right exists only where law names a claimant, a duty-bearer and a remedy.
Moral: a right is justified by ethical reasoning before, and independently of, enactment.

groups.heading: WHAT EACH GROUND DELIVERS
items: Locke makes government a fiduciary trust whose breach forfeits authority and licenses resistance.
Bentham makes rights the children of law and dismisses natural rights as nonsense upon stilts.
The moral register alone explains anti-slavery and anti-colonial claims voiced before legal recognition.

groups.heading: PRESUPPOSITIONS, TRAP AND VERDICT
items: Presuppositions: intrinsic moral status, institutional enforceability, and justice not exhausted by positive law.
Trap: Bentham rejects natural rights, not legal rights, and legal validity is never moral legitimacy.
Verdict: a mature order needs all three registers — nature grounds, law enforces, morality judges.

stages.mechanism_strip: Each theory answers the question why is this owed differently: nature confers standing before government exists, positive law confers an enforceable position with a remedy, and morality confers a critical standard against what the law has actually enacted.
stages.answer_line: The first mark on any rights stem is earned by refusing to treat every urgent interest as a right: a right is a justified claim, liberty, power or immunity, and a controlled answer names its ground as natural, legal or moral before it argues about anything else.

stages.title: THE STRUCTURE OF A RIGHT AND THE CORRELATIVITY VERDICT
sequence: Four incidents, only one strict correlative
Will theory against interest theory
Mixed account covers agency and welfare
Universality of aspiration, plurality of articulation
Correlativity is necessary, but not identity
matrix: no positive duty to assist me

groups.heading: THE FOUR JURAL INCIDENTS
items: Claim-right correlates with duty; only here does a strict duty-partner exist.
Liberty correlates with no-right and imposes no positive duty to assist the holder.
Power correlates with liability, and immunity correlates with disability.

groups.heading: WHAT A RIGHT PROTECTS
items: Will theory: the right-holder controls another's duty; it fits autonomy but handles children badly.
Interest theory: the right protects a vital interest; it fits welfare but can underplay agency.
Most working systems run a mixed account of agency and well-being together.

groups.heading: HOW FAR THE RIGHT TRAVELS
items: Universalist: equal worth and protection from cruelty are a common human aspiration.
Relativist: personhood, authority and obligation are read through particular traditions.
Verdict: correlativity is conceptual for claim-rights and institutional for the rest, never a logical identity.

stages.mechanism_strip: Separating the four incidents shows exactly where a duty-partner is entailed and where it is not, so the correlativity question is settled by analysis of jural positions instead of by slogan.
stages.answer_line: Correlativity is the mark-bearing device on this clause: claim-rights are necessarily correlative to duties while liberties are not, so the slogan that rights and duties are two sides of one coin is exact for one Hohfeldian incident and merely loose about the rest.

stages.title: DUTIES, THE INVERSION OF THE USUAL ORDER, AND THE PRIORITY VERDICT

pills.text: PERFORM THE DUTY, EARN THE RIGHT

sequence: Duty is what is owed, not mere obedience
Legal duty carries sanction and remedy
Moral duty binds in conscience
Gandhi inverts the order: duty earns the right
Verdict: co-originality with a sequencing caveat
matrix: the person is protected against coercion
rights and duties are mutually sustaining
best fit for a constitutional democracy

groups.heading: TWO KINDS OF DUTY
items: Legal duty rests on law, constitution and statute, and carries a sanction and a remedy.
Moral duty rests on conscience and ethical reason, enforced by praise, blame and public criticism.
Law cannot codify the whole of ethical life, so citizenship depends on habits law alone cannot manufacture.

groups.heading: GANDHI'S INVERSION AND THE INDIAN TEXT
items: Perform the duty and the right follows: the true source of rights is duty, secured by service and self-restraint.
Self-rule (swaraj) begins with rule over oneself, so the duties run to conscience and community rather than to the state.
Article 51A, inserted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, is non-justiciable exhortation.

groups.heading: THE PRIORITY DEBATE AND ITS VERDICT
items: Rights-first shields dissent and minorities but risks an atomised entitlement culture.
Duty-first revives reciprocity but can postpone the claims of the powerless.
Verdict: co-originality with a sequencing caveat — foreground duty if the culture requires it, never demote rights.

stages.mechanism_strip: Duties convert abstract norms into expectations of conduct, so a claim-right becomes socially effective only when some determinate agent is bound to respect it, protect it or provide for it.
stages.answer_line: A duty is not the same thing as obedience, and the defensible verdict on the priority question is co-originality with a sequencing caveat: duty may be foregrounded pedagogically in a culture of entitlement without ever demoting rights to conditional grants.

stages.title: ACCOUNTABILITY: THREE CHANNELS AND THE DIRECTION THE EXAMINER TESTS

pills.text: RULE OF LAW AND JUDICIAL REVIEW

sequence: The state claims coercive authority over persons
Political channel: rulers can be removed
Legal channel: rulers under reviewable law
Moral channel: shareable public reasons
Verdict: reciprocal, never one-way answerability

groups.heading: THREE CHANNELS OF ANSWERABILITY
items: Political: elections, opposition, legislature and a free press let citizens remove rulers.
Legal: rule of law, judicial review, due process and remedy put rulers under the law.
Moral: public reason and the dignity of the governed require shareable justifications.

groups.heading: WHY THE CHANNELS MATTER TOGETHER
items: Together the three channels convert coercive power into authority.
Remove all three and what remains is domination rather than government.
Elections alone deliver formal answerability alongside substantive domination.

groups.heading: THE DIRECTION CORRECTION
items: A stem may assume citizens answer to the state; rights principally make the state answerable to citizens.
Concede that rights also generate responsibilities, such as the duty not to defame that accompanies free speech.
Verdict: reciprocal accountability; keep answering for power apart from the duties that accompany a right.

stages.mechanism_strip: Because the state claims coercive authority over persons, every exercise of that authority must be explicable to those bound by it, and the three channels convert power into authority by making removal, review and public justification possible.
stages.answer_line: Accountability is the institutional cash value of the distinction between authority and force: rights principally make the state answerable to citizens, and only derivatively generate the responsibilities that accompany the exercise of those same rights.

stages.title: LIBERAL, IDEALIST AND CONTRACTARIAN PICTURES OF THE SAME RELATION

pills.text: STATE FORCED TO BE FREE WITH CONDITIONS

sequence: Name the state-of-nature premise first
Hobbes: security bought with near-total transfer
Locke: limited government held as fiduciary trust
Rousseau: general will and civic freedom
Verdict: grounds limits, abstracts from inequality
matrix: near-total power to one sovereign for security
natural law governs; rights precede government
limited government held as a fiduciary trust

groups.heading: THREE STATES OF NATURE, THREE BARGAINS
items: Hobbes: war of all against all, near-total transfer for security, resistance confined to self-preservation.
Locke: a state of nature governed by natural law, limited government as fiduciary trust, resistance on breach.
Rousseau: freedom corrupted by inequality, surrender to the general will, and self-rule through it.

groups.heading: THREE DIRECTIONS OF EXPLANATION
items: Liberal: the person is prior and the state instrumental, with the standing risk of atomism.
Idealist: family and civil society culminate in the state as ethical life, with Green removing hindrances to self-realisation.
Marxist as relation-theory: the state is a class instrument and formal rights can mask real unfreedom.

groups.heading: HINGE PROBLEM AND ADEQUACY VERDICT
items: Rousseau's forced to be free is defensible only with equality, generality of law and the absence of factions.
The deal always follows from the diagnosis: change the premise and the state changes with it.
Contract grounds limits and consent, yet abstracts from real inequality, so human rights need a further ground.

stages.mechanism_strip: Contract theory replaces divine right and conquest with a justificatory story addressed to rational persons, so legitimacy is tested by what free and equal contractors could reasonably be expected to accept.
stages.answer_line: In every contract stem the deal follows from the diagnosis: name the state of nature first as war of all against all, as inconvenient but norm-governed, or as free but corrupted, and Hobbes's sovereign, Locke's trust and Rousseau's general will follow almost automatically.

stages.title: RADICAL AND SITUATED CRITIQUES AND THE UNCONDITIONAL-RIGHTS CHARGE

pills.text: JUSTIFY COERCION, DO NOT ASSUME IT
BOUNDED RIGHTS DO NOT ENTAIL ANARCHY

sequence: Anarchism: justify coercion, do not assume it
Marxism: formal rights can mask material domination
Welfare, communitarian and feminist corrections
Unconditional is not the same as inalienable
Bounded rights do not entail anarchy
matrix: the right to rule is presumptively illegitimate
adjudication, defence and coordination at scale
formal rights coexist with material domination
formal liberty is empty without means
positive freedom and a social minimum
the abstract self hides embeddedness and private power
membership, common goods, care and dependence
must still protect dissent and minority rights

groups.heading: ATTACKS ON THE COERCIVE STATE
items: Philosophical anarchism treats the state's right to rule as presumptively illegitimate and cooperation as voluntary.
Its limits are feasibility, impartial adjudication, external defence and large-scale coordination.
Gandhi's ever-widening circles keep the individual at the centre, each outer ring serving the inner.

groups.heading: ATTACKS ON THE ABSTRACT INDIVIDUAL
items: Marxist: equal legal rights can coexist with deep material domination, so formal freedom may mask class power.
Welfare: formal liberty is empty without means, so a social minimum enlarges effective freedom.
Communitarian and feminist: the self is socially constituted, and the private sphere hides dependence and power.

groups.heading: THE UNCONDITIONAL-RIGHTS CHARGE
items: Distinguish unconditional from inalienable: rights are inalienable yet limitable.
Internal limits are the equal rights of others, harm constraints, public order and institutional adjudication.
Verdict: bounded rights do not entail anarchy; only a naive absolutism about rights ever would.

stages.mechanism_strip: Each critique isolates one assumption the standard justification makes, that coercion is necessary, that formal liberty suffices, or that the self is pre-social, and then denies precisely that assumption.
stages.answer_line: The decisive move against the anarchy charge is a distinction between unconditional and inalienable: rights are inalienable yet limitable, so bounded rights carrying internal harm-limits and correlative duties do not entail anarchy, and only a naive absolutism about rights ever would.

stages.title: POLITICAL OBLIGATION: SIX GROUNDS DRIVEN THROUGH FOUR TESTS

pills.text: PRINCIPLES, HARD CASES, RIGHTS AS TRUMPS
BEING OBLIGED IS NOT HAVING AN OBLIGATION

sequence: Is there a moral duty to obey because it is law?
Six grounds: consent, fair play, natural duty, association
Gratitude, and the philosophical-anarchist denial
Four tests: generality, particularity, content-independence, defeasibility
Raz on authority, Dworkin on principles and trumps
matrix: generality: tacit consent is not voluntary
accept the benefits, owe a share of the burdens
support just institutions that apply to you
particularity: why this state rather than any?
obligation flows from membership or benefaction
no general duty has yet been established
cannot distinguish the state from a private agency

groups.heading: SIX CANDIDATE GROUNDS
items: Consent (Locke, Hobbes, Rousseau) and fair play (Hart, Rawls) derive the duty from what the citizen has done.
Natural duty of justice (Rawls), associative obligation (Dworkin) and gratitude derive it from what the citizen is in.
Philosophical anarchism (Wolff, Simmons) denies that any ground has yet established a general duty.

groups.heading: FOUR TESTS AND WHERE EACH GROUND BREAKS
items: Generality and particularity: a natural duty binds me to any just state rather than distinctively to my own.
Content-independence: obedience must follow because the law directs it, not because I independently agree.
Defeasibility: fair play collapses where the benefits of public order are unavoidable and non-excludable (Nozick).

groups.heading: AUTHORITY, PRINCIPLES AND THE TRAP
items: Raz's service conception: authority is legitimate when its directives are pre-emptive reasons that improve conformity.
Dworkin, Taking Rights Seriously, 1977: principles have weight, hard cases turn on them, and rights are trumps.
Trap: never give the service conception to Simmons, or philosophical anarchism to Raz.

stages.mechanism_strip: Being obliged by fear and having an obligation are different things, so a genuine obligation must direct obedience because the law directs it, which is exactly what the content-independence test measures.
stages.answer_line: Obedience is never self-evident, and the mark-bearing move is to say which ground the stem assumes and which test that ground fails, because being obliged by a gunman and having an obligation to the state are two entirely different things.

stages.title: THE LADDER OF REFUSAL AND THE INDIAN CONSTITUTIONAL LIMIT

pills.text: NO RIGHT TO BREAK THE LAW

sequence: A defeasible duty makes refusal graded, not binary
Legal dissent within the law
Conscientious objection seeks personal exemption
Civil disobedience: public, non-violent, penalty-accepting
Resistance and revolution carry the gravest burden

groups.heading: FOUR RUNGS OF REFUSAL
items: Legal dissent works within the law through speech, vote, petition and litigation.
Conscientious objection seeks a personal exemption, may be private, and accepts the penalty.
Civil disobedience is a public, non-violent, penalty-accepting breach; resistance and revolution go further.

groups.heading: CONDITIONS FOR THE THIRD RUNG
items: The law must be seriously unjust and legal channels exhausted, blocked or unavailable to the affected group.
The breach must be open and non-violent, and the legal penalty must be accepted.
Rawls adds that the society must be nearly just and its majority capable of being persuaded.

groups.heading: ANCHORS AND THE INDIAN LIMIT
items: Thoreau, Civil Disobedience, 1849, is individual refusal rather than an organised mass campaign.
Salt Satyagraha, 1930, is announced, non-violent and arrest-accepting; Ambedkar, 25 November 1949, names the grammar of anarchy.
Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) protect protest subject to reasonable restrictions; there is no right to break the law.

stages.mechanism_strip: Publicity, non-violence, exhaustion of legal channels and acceptance of the penalty operate as severe filters, so a defeasible obligation can be overridden in a particular case without dissolving legal order in general.
stages.answer_line: Civil disobedience is defined by two features ordinary law-breaking lacks, a public appeal to shared principles and acceptance of the legal penalty, and it is precisely that penalty-acceptance which demonstrates fidelity to law as such while one particular law is contested.

stages.title: THE ANSWER ENGINE: STAGED DEBATES, TRAP BANK AND THE GRADED VERDICT

pills.text: DEFINE, LOCATE, RIVALS, OBJECT, EVIDENCE, VERDICT
ARISTOTLE AGAINST PLATO ON THE MIDDLE

sequence: Define the stem's key term precisely
Locate the case on the relation spectrum
State the rivals and stage one real debate
Voice the objection to your own thesis
Close with a graded, specified verdict

groups.heading: THE SIX-MOVE ANSWER SPINE
items: Define the stem's key term, then locate the case on the relation spectrum.
State the rivals in play, then run one objection and reply on the strongest of them.
Cite India-centric evidence by position, then deliver a graded verdict rather than a winner.

groups.heading: DEBATES WORTH STAGING
items: Hobbes against Locke on resistance; Locke against Rousseau on the will.
Liberal against communitarian on the self; liberal against idealist on freedom.
Gandhi against Western anarchism; Aristotle against Plato on the statism and individualism axis.

groups.heading: TRAP BANK AND CLOSING VERDICT
items: State is not government; Bentham is not anti-all-rights; Article 51A is not enforceable.
India has constitutional supremacy, not parliamentary sovereignty; never fabricate a case, article, quotation or date.
Close by specifying the justified balance of dignity, justice and order rather than asserting it.

stages.mechanism_strip: A twenty-marker is won in the fourth and fifth paragraphs, where a real debate is staged and the strongest criticism of one's own side is voiced before any verdict is offered.
stages.answer_line: The individual is neither an atom standing outside society nor a cell inside the state, so the examiner rewards a specified balance of dignity, justice and order that is argued through one staged debate and one honest concession rather than merely asserted.
